truth: Solstheim is a cold island off Skyrim's north-east coast that Red Mountain's ash has half buried. A mountain massif runs through its middle: south of it the ground is a low plain of ash under a falling grey sky, north of it spruce, glacier and sea ice. The Skaal hunters of the north-east keep a covenant with the All-Maker and six standing stones; the south belongs to Red Year Dunmer refugees who hold Raven Rock's failing ebony mine against ash storms and ash spawn. Between them rise a dragon-cult temple, Dwemer ruins, Nordic barrows and a Telvanni mushroom tower, while something in the central temple has begun to dream again.

skaal.truth: The north-east and east of the island belong to the Skaal, hunters and tellers who keep an old covenant with the All-Maker: they take what the land lends, work stalhrim and bone and read the six stones as a living calendar. Their village is a ring of hide-and-bone houses round a fire and a stone circle, with no streets and no coin. Beside them Nord hunting bands keep Thirsk's single great hall against riekling raids, and reavers have taken a lodge on the shore. The Skaal are losing: the stones sicken, the young leave for Raven Rock's wages, and the colony wants their timber.

raven_rock.truth: Raven Rock is a refugee town behind a bulwark. Dunmer who fled Red Mountain's eruption took over the East Empire Company's failing ebony mine on the south-west bay and walled it against ash storms and the ash spawn that walk out of them. A Redoran council and a guard captain ration the grain, the shaft is nearly worked out, a hall of the Temple keeps the faith, and the dead go into the ash because the family tombs are across the sea. The harbour is the island's only ferry landing and the colony's only link to the world.

moesring.truth: The Moesring massif is the island's spine and its dividing line: ash falls on its southern foot, snow on its north, and a belt of grey sleet marks where they meet. It carries the island's oldest layers: a dragon-cult temple whose stair climbs from an altar of the old kings to a sunken sanctum, barrows of thane-kings, Dwemer works and an observatory on a ridge. Its pass is the only low way between north and south, and everything the colony and the Skaal want from each other must cross it.

isinfier.truth: South and east of the mountain lies a plain of ash: drifts, charred stumps, cliff racers and netch overhead and ash spawn after dark. A Telvanni master keeps a lone mushroom tower and a spore garden on its south-east point; an Imperial fort and a ruined mage-citadel watch the sea road; a Dwemer city half sunk in ice lies on the east shore and a trader's shack sells to anyone. The farms that survive here are measured in fields, and grow in ash that nothing should grow in.

felsaad.truth: The north and north-west coast is cliffs, ice fog and a glacier tongue, the cold end of the island. Rieklings hold its caves and shore camps in numbers found nowhere else, riding boars and throwing spears, and a mine is theirs by raid. Stalhrim forms at the glacier's foot where a spring freezes over its vein, and a giant's frozen castle stands above the sea. Ships rarely land and the winter closes the coast entirely; the only landing is a half-wrecked jetty.

brodir.truth: On the ash plain's western edge a ring of ash-trees stands green while the ground round it is grey: a spring beneath them the fall does not foul. It is the island's last stand of living broadleaf, the source of the seed stock the colony's farms depend on, and a place the Dunmer refugees hold as ground where the dead rest. A keeper who answers every question with a question tends it; a mage's tower on the ridge above watches without help.

bloodskal.truth: The western ridge between the colony and the mountain is barrow country: Bloodskal Barrow, the grave of a hero whose blade is the island's best-known relic, a hunter's lodge where footprints go in and none come out, a flooded and ash-choked mine, and a peak with a bear that does not belong. It is where the colony's quarrymen go to dig and where the old Nord settlers lie. Everything here is a question of who owns a grave: the colony wants the barrow's stone, the Skaal want the dead undisturbed, and the dead have views of their own.
